book_title: Stampede and the Westness of West
subject_line: The Stampede and the westness of Calgary
email_body:
Dear Aritha,

I have been reading about Stampede and the Westness of West, and how you turn the rodeo into a question about who Calgary thinks it is. Your essay on what the Stampede means to Calgarians made me curious about the line you walk between affection and critique.

I would like to ask how you decided on a form that sits between prose and poetry for a subject so loud and public.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is built from a few written questions you can answer at your own pace, and you see the full text for review before anything is published.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: Des Corps extraterrestres à Listening for Jupiter
email_body:
Bonjour Pierre-Luc,

En lisant sur Les corps extraterrestres, votre deuxième roman paru chez Druide, j'ai été frappé par son parcours : c'est aussi le premier de vos livres à exister en anglais, sous le titre Listening for Jupiter. Et vous écrivez aujourd'hui des romans, des essais et des textes hybrides depuis Victoria.

J'aimerais vous demander ce que la traduction vous a révélé sur ce roman, et si écrire en français en Colombie-Britannique change votre rapport à la langue.

The Author Ledger est un projet indépendant qui publie de courts portraits d'auteurs. Chaque portrait se construit à partir de quelques questions écrites, auxquelles vous répondez à votre rythme, et le texte complet vous est soumis pour relecture avant publication.

Seriez-vous partant ? Aucune obligation.

Bien cordialement,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Two novels with Éditions Druide (L'équation du temps 2013, Les corps extraterrestres 2015); second novel translated as Listening for Jupiter (Erudit bio note, All Lit Up); UVic French faculty. Email on UVic faculty profile, email seen in search result.

subject_line: From Wolf Tree to In the Tiger Park
email_body:
Dear Alison,

Your poetry runs from Wolf Tree, which won two Manitoba Book Awards, to In the Tiger Park. Animals sit at the centre of both titles, and the Jacket2 piece on In the Tiger Park made me curious about how the prairie and the wild sit together in your work.

I would like to ask what drew you to that tiger park as a frame for a whole book.
